metadata.title: Claude, Brief Section Drafter.
metadata.purpose: Take apart the brief-section-drafter skill and judge the design: what it actually does (draft one section to a spec, every time), and what it deliberately leaves to the human (checking facts, cases, and anything outside that spec).
metadata.one_flag: N/A — every claim in this reel is a confirmed, present-tense description of what the skill does, not an inference

beats.narration_text: The honest wrong guess someone typed: Claude WRITE my legal brief. Not quite — it drafts one section, held to your case theory. Every fact and every citation is still on you. Here's what's actually happening.

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Writer types the newcomer's wrong-guess word 'WRITE' (implying Claude produces the whole finished brief), hesitates, corrects to 'draft' -> lands the real question. The wrong guess is picked up directly by B03's stated scope (one section, house style, case theory). Narration is 35 words + lead_silence_s 0.8, giving the typing a >=9s window (TIMING LAW).

beats.narration_text: Here's the machinery. A skill is a folder Claude reads before it does anything. This one — brief-section-drafter — is one file, SKILL.md, plain English, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. Legibility over cleverness: the whole instruction set fits on a page you can audit.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — linear, no branching unless a step says branch. Predictability over cleverness: trace the whole run before it happens.

Here's the interesting constraint. Draft one section, in house style, consistent with your case theory — every fact cited, every case pinned, every argument tied back to that theory. Stay inside that scope and the section holds its shape every run. They optimized for reproducibility at the expense of reach: it won't draft the whole brief, but what it does draft looks the same every time.

props.heading: The interesting constraint.
props.body: One section: house style, case theory, every fact and case cited.
props.sparkLine: Reproducibility over reach — same shape, every run.

beats.narration_text: Same spec in, same section out, every time. Checking the facts, the cases, and anything outside that spec — that's still your job, by design.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. I'm drafting the argument section of a brief; I have my case theory and every source ready. Read the brief-section-drafter skill, tell me exactly what facts and cases you need before I draft a single sentence, then draft the section in house style — citing every fact and every case as you go. Go deeper: what changes if the case theory shifts? Draft both versions side by side, and mark every place the change forces a different citation.
